title: China port fee reprieve and Asia-US rate outlook for Q4
metaDescription: Port fees on Chinese-built ships delayed until January. Transpacific spot rates breach $10,000 to USEC. Rate hikes likely in early October.
bottomLine: The Trump administration extended its suspension of port fees on Chinese-built vessels until 10 January 2027, giving you two months of breathing room before shipping costs rise again. Transpacific spot rates hit $11,445 per FEU to the US east coast this week and analysts expect another uptick in early October before Golden Week capacity comes back.

stories.headline: Port fees on Chinese-built ships delayed until 10 January
stories.tldr: Trump and Xi agreed to extend the suspension of port fees on Chinese-built vessels by two months to 10 January 2027.
stories.whatHappened:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced on 24 September that the US and China agreed to extend their trade-war truce by two months to 10 January 2027. The extension covers the suspension of port fees that would apply to vessels built in Chinese shipyards calling at US ports.

The reprieve follows a letter signed by 238 trade groups urging the US Trade Representative to extend the suspension. The Trump administration had originally planned to release a report on alleged excess capacity before the Xi-Trump summit that would recommend a 7.5 per cent tariff on Chinese goods.
stories.whyItMatters:
You have until 10 January to ship goods on the same vessel economics you see today. After that date, expect carriers to pass through the port fee as a surcharge on every container arriving in the US, whether the vessel was built in China or not. Carriers bundle costs, they do not itemise them by ship.

The two-month window matters most if you are tendering for 2027 contract rates right now. Your forwarder cannot give you a clean rate card when a fee structure resets in January. Either lock a rate that absorbs the fee for the full year, or accept a rate-review clause that lets the carrier reprice in Q1. Neither option is comfortable, but the second one at least keeps you competitive through peak.

If you have stock on the water now, this does not change your cost. If you are booking October sailings, factor in the 10 January deadline for any follow-up orders. A 40-day transit plus dwell puts a late-November sailing at risk of landing after the fees return.
stories.hotTake: A two-month extension is not a resolution, it is a placeholder. The port fee will come back, and when it does, carriers will apply it to every sailing regardless of where the ship was built, because that is how maritime cost absorption works. Book your Q1 volumes now or accept that you are repricing in January.
actions: Lock contract rates for Q1 2027 shipments before the 10 January deadline or negotiate a rate-review clause.
Pull forward any January orders to ship before the port fee suspension ends.
Ask your forwarder for a landed-cost scenario with and without the port fee applied.

stories.headline: Transpacific spot rates breach $10,000 to USEC, Q4 climb expected
stories.tldr: Spot rates from Asia to the US east coast hit $11,445 per FEU this week, with early October likely to bring another rate increase.
stories.whatHappened:
Spot rates from Asia to the US east coast reached $11,445 per 40ft container this week on Drewry's World Container Index, breaching $10,000 for the first time since the late peak season rally began in late August. Rates to the US west coast stand at $8,255 per FEU.

Xeneta data shows shippers are now paying $2,691 more per FEU to the east coast and $1,280 more to the west coast compared to 1 July, increases of 31 per cent and 18 per cent respectively. Chief analyst Peter Sand said the rising trend may begin to tail off in the first half of October, but expects a short pause before resumption.
stories.whyItMatters:
If you are booking space for October delivery, you are paying peak rates on a lane that was supposed to be softening by now. The $11,445 rate to the east coast is not a short-term blip, it is what carriers can command when vessel capacity is tight and Chinese exporters are frontloading ahead of tariff risk.

Your landed cost just took a 31 per cent hit on the transpacific if you are on the spot market. Even if you have a contract rate, expect your forwarder to invoke a peak season surcharge or a space guarantee fee to secure equipment. Carriers are not allocating boxes to contracted cargo when they can sell the same slot at spot rates.

October bookings face two pressures. Golden Week begins on 1 October, pulling capacity out of the market for a week. When sailings resume, you are competing with everyone who delayed their September orders to avoid the current rate spike. That is not a formula for falling prices. Xeneta is calling for rates to pause, not drop, and a pause at $11,445 is still a problem for your margin.
stories.hotTake: The market is pricing in tariff risk that may or may not land in January. You are paying for other people's nervousness. If your product category is not on the Section 301 list, you are subsidising someone else's front-loading. Book now anyway, because waiting does not make space cheaper in Q4.
actions: Lock space for November and December shipments now, even at elevated rates, rather than waiting for a correction that may not come.
Pull your Q4 air-freight trigger price down to $6 per kg, because the sea-air cost gap is narrowing fast.
Run a scenario where your Q4 ocean cost stays at current levels through year-end and adjust your retail price or promotional calendar accordingly.

stories.headline: Asia-Europe rates down 38% since July, but pause expected in October
stories.tldr: Spot rates from Asia to the Mediterranean fell 38 per cent since 1 July, but Xeneta expects the decline to pause in early October.
stories.whatHappened:
Container spot rates from the Far East to the Mediterranean dropped to $4,369 per FEU as of 24 September, down 38 per cent from 1 July, according to Xeneta. Rates to North Europe fell 29 per cent in the same period to $3,945 per FEU, a decline of $1,590 per FEU.

Peter Sand said early October may provide a short pause before the falling trend resumes. The softening on Europe lanes contrasts sharply with the transpacific, where rates have climbed consistently since late August.
stories.whyItMatters:
If you sell into Europe, your ocean freight cost has dropped by more than a third in three months. That is a margin opportunity if you locked a higher rate earlier in the year, or a chance to undercut competitors who are still working through inventory shipped at July rates.

The October pause matters because it signals the floor. Xeneta is not calling for rates to keep falling through Q4, they are calling for stabilisation and then a possible resumption of declines. That means if you are tendering for 2027 contracts now, you have leverage. Carriers cannot point to a rising spot market to justify a higher base rate on Europe lanes.

The pause also tells you where to allocate product geographically. If you can route goods to either the US or Europe, the Europe lane is $7,076 per FEU cheaper to the east coast right now. For bulky, low-margin goods where freight is a large share of landed cost, that gap may flip the business case for which market to prioritise in Q4.
stories.hotTake: A 38 per cent rate drop in three months is not a discount, it is a market correction after carriers overshot on capacity and pricing. The pause in October is carriers testing whether they can hold the line. They cannot, because the volume is not there. Rates will resume falling, but slowly.
actions: Tender your 2027 Europe contract rates now while spot rates are down and carriers are nervous about volume.
Shift Q4 promotional inventory toward Europe if you sell in both regions and your product can absorb the longer lead time.
Rebook any October Europe shipments to capture the current rate before the pause firms up.

contentHooks: Port fees on Chinese-built ships delayed until 10 January, but that is a placeholder not a resolution.
Transpacific spot rates hit $11,445 to the east coast, up 31% since 1 July, and Q4 is not softening.
You are paying $2,691 more per FEU to the US east coast than you were in July, and October will not fix it.
Asia-Europe rates dropped 38% in three months, creating a $7,076 per FEU gap between Europe and the US east coast.
Chinese ports moved a record 7.3 million TEU in the week to 20 September, exporters frontloading ahead of tariff risk.
Golden Week pulls capacity out of the market on 1 October, right when everyone who delayed September orders comes back.
Xeneta is calling for a pause in early October, not a drop, and a pause at $11,445 is still a margin problem.
Carriers are prioritising spot-market cargo over contracted boxes because they can command peak rates through Q4.
The two-month port fee extension gives you until 10 January to lock Q1 contract rates before the cost base resets.
If your product is not on the Section 301 list, you are subsidising other sellers' frontloading by paying elevated spot rates.
Asia-Europe lanes are $7,076 cheaper per FEU than Asia-USEC right now, enough to flip your geographic allocation for Q4.

faq.question: When do port fees on Chinese-built ships come back?
faq.answer: The suspension ends on 10 January 2027. After that date, the US is expected to impose port fees on vessels built in Chinese shipyards calling at US ports. Carriers will pass the cost through as a surcharge on all containers, regardless of which ship carries your goods. You have until 10 January to ship at current vessel economics. If you are booking Q1 2027 volumes now, either lock a rate that absorbs the fee or negotiate a rate-review clause for January.

faq.question: Why are Asia-US rates still climbing in late September?
faq.answer: Spot rates from Asia to the US east coast hit $11,445 per FEU this week, up 31 per cent since 1 July. The increase reflects tight vessel capacity, Chinese exporters frontloading goods ahead of potential tariff announcements, and carriers prioritising spot-market cargo over contracted boxes. Golden Week begins on 1 October, pulling capacity out for a week, which will keep rates elevated into early October.

faq.question: Should I book ocean freight now or wait for Q4 rates to drop?
faq.answer: Book now. Transpacific spot rates are at $11,445 per FEU to the US east coast and Xeneta expects rates to pause in early October, not drop. Golden Week starts on 1 October, reducing available capacity. Carriers are not allocating space to contracted cargo when they can sell the same slot at spot rates. Waiting will not make space cheaper. If you sell into Europe, rates have fallen 38 per cent since July, so tender your 2027 contract now.

faq.question: How much more am I paying for ocean freight to the US compared to July?
faq.answer: You are paying $2,691 more per FEU to the US east coast and $1,280 more to the west coast compared to 1 July, increases of 31 per cent and 18 per cent respectively. Current spot rates are $11,445 per FEU to the east coast and $8,255 to the west coast. If you have a contract rate, expect peak season surcharges or space guarantee fees to secure equipment.

faq.question: What happens to my shipping cost after the port fee suspension ends in January?
faq.answer: After 10 January 2027, carriers will apply port fees to all US-bound containers, whether your specific ship was built in China or not. Carriers bundle costs across their fleet rather than itemising by vessel. Expect the fee to appear as a new surcharge line on your invoice. If you are tendering 2027 contract rates now, either lock a rate that includes the fee or accept a rate-review clause that lets the carrier reprice in Q1.
